structuralDecisions.decision: Fix both fragile locators in place using the existing flat `[data-testid="..."]` pattern already dominant in CartPage.ts and HomePage.ts — no new selector strategy, base class, or package.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Confirmed by reading both files: every other registerElement/locator call in CartPage.ts and HomePage.ts already uses a flat data-testid attribute selector. The two violations (CartPage.ts:22 has-text, HomePage.ts:39 nested selector) are exceptions to an established pattern, not evidence a new pattern is needed. This is additive-within-pattern per the architect invocation criteria — no layer boundary, package, or abstraction decision is actually in play here.
tradeOffs: None material — confirmed by direct file inspection rather than assumed.

structuralDecisions.decision: Rename CartView.vue's complete-transaction button test id from `checkout-btn` to `complete-transaction-btn` in place, rather than adding a second, parallel test id.
structuralDecisions.rationale: grep confirms `checkout-btn` has exactly one occurrence repo-wide (CartView.vue:61). A rename is safe and leaves no stale attribute that could silently reattract a future locator.
tradeOffs: None — single call site verified by grep before deciding.

structuralDecisions.decision: Point HomePage.ts's clickFirstProductDetails() at the existing `item-name` test id (already rendered by ItemCard.vue) instead of inventing a new, purpose-built test id for the details link.
structuralDecisions.rationale: ItemCard.vue:26 already renders data-testid="item-name" on a router-link to the same /item/:id destination the current nested selector `[data-testid="item-card"] a` resolves to. Reusing it is behavior-preserving and avoids a redundant attribute on markup that already has an addressable id.
tradeOffs: The locator's semantic intent (navigate to product details) is now carried by an attribute named after the item's name text rather than its own purpose — acceptable: a third testid on the same anchor would duplicate markup for no behavioral gain.
